title: Bruno (6 October)
hook: a famous teacher walks away into the mountains and founds an order of silence
carry: the cross stands while the world turns

segments.voice: Yesterday, the guardian angels, and Rhoda leaving Peter at the gate. Your line was beside you. Who did you stay near? Day one thousand thirty-three.

A man at the top of his field. He runs a cathedral school, his students go on to high office, and one of them will one day become pope. People expect him to rise. Instead, he and a few companions walk up into the mountains above Grenoble, into a wild valley, and build huts. No lecture hall, no audience, almost no talking. Just prayer and work and silence. The place gave its name to a way of life. Today's word is that name.
screen: `A TEACHER AT THE TOP.` → `UP INTO THE MOUNTAINS.` → `A VALLEY OF SILENCE.`

segments.voice: The word is Carthusian. It names the monks and nuns who follow the way Saint Bruno began in those mountains, called the Chartreuse. Bruno had been a respected teacher at Reims, in France. Tradition says he grew sick of the politics and money around him and wanted God alone. The local bishop, Hugh, gave him and his companions the land, and they built a hermitage there: the Grande Chartreuse. Here's how a Carthusian lives, then and now. Each monk has his own cell, really a small house with a garden and a workshop. He prays, reads, works and eats there, mostly alone. The monks come together in church for the long night prayers and for Mass, and on certain days they share a meal and a walk. Silence runs through the whole day. Not silence as a punishment. Silence as room to listen. The Douay-Rheims gives a psalm line they could take as a rule: "Be still and see that I am God." Bruno himself didn't get to stay. His old student became Pope Urban the Second and called him to Rome as an adviser. Bruno went, obeyed, and then asked to leave. He founded another hermitage in Calabria, in southern Italy, and died there. The Carthusians' motto, in Latin, is Stat crux dum volvitur orbis: the cross stands while the world turns. Bruno himself was pulled down the mountain and never lived there again. Up in the cells he left behind, the same prayer went on.
screen: `BRUNO LEAVES A BRILLIANT CAREER.` · `A CELL, A GARDEN, A WORKSHOP.` · `BE STILL AND SEE THAT I AM GOD.` · `THE CROSS STANDS WHILE THE WORLD TURNS.` · then, large: `STAT CRUX DUM VOLVITUR ORBIS.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: keep silent. For these two minutes, no words at all, not even in your head if you can manage it. Sit, breathe, and when a sentence starts forming, let it go unfinished. Notice how much of your mind is talk. If you pray, you can hold the psalm line, be still, and let the rest fall quiet. If you don't, simply rest in the quiet. And sometime later today, if you can, try ten minutes. The bell holds the time.
Carthusian. A monk or nun of the order Saint Bruno began in the Chartreuse mountains: a life of cells, night prayer and silence.
Your line: the cross stands while the world turns. Today, when the news spins fast, pick one fixed thing, a prayer, a breath, a walk, and let it stand still. Day one thousand thirty-three.

howItsDone: Saint Bruno is remembered on 6 October; Carthusian monks and nuns keep it as their founder's feast inside their charterhouses, which the public generally does not visit.

notes: Bruno at Reims, Hugh of Grenoble giving land, Urban II as former student, death in Calabria: standard biography; confirm.
'Tradition says he grew sick of the politics and money around him': a summary of the traditional account (troubles under Archbishop Manasses); confirm framing.
Description of Carthusian daily life (cells with garden and workshop, night office, shared meal and walk on certain days): confirm it reflects current Statutes.
The index hook says 'unchanged for nine centuries'; that claim is omitted under the claims rule.
Psalm 45:11 in Douay-Rheims numbering (46:10 Hebrew); confirm exact Challoner wording.
Trapdoor 'a liqueur' refers to Chartreuse made by the monks; confirm tone is fine.
Latin pronunciation guide is ecclesiastical-ish; confirm.

Editor: replaced two stock lines ('silence is the air they breathe'; 'popes come and go, empires rise and fall') with concrete detail from Bruno's own story; 'the same prayer went on' after he left is a reasonable reading of the community continuing, Keeper to confirm.
Audit: 'sent on to Calabria' was wrong; Bruno asked to leave Rome and chose Calabria himself (the teach already says so); the line now says only that he never lived at the Chartreuse again.
